questions.question: In a circle with centre $O$, the central angle $AOB$ is $60°$. If the radius of the circle is 12 cm, what is the length of the chord $AB$?

solution.content: **Observe the triangle $\triangle AOB$:** $OA = OB = 12$ cm (both radii), and $\angle AOB = 60°$.

**Recognise an equilateral triangle:** If two sides are equal and the included angle is $60°$, the third angle is also $60°$ (since $180° - 60° = 120°$ split equally). So $\triangle AOB$ is equilateral.
**Conclusion:** All sides are equal, so $AB = OA = OB = 12$ cm.

questions.answer: AB = 12 cm (the triangle AOB is equilateral).

questions.question: Let $A$ and $B$ be two points on a circle with centre $O$. **(i)** Are there points $X$, $Y$ on the circle, on the same side of $AB$, such that $\angle AXB$ is different from $\angle AYB$? **(ii)** Is it true that if $\angle AXB = \angle AYB$, then $X$ and $Y$ lie on the same side of the circle? **(iii)** If $\angle AXB = \angle AYB$, and $X$ and $Y$ do not lie on the circle, does the circle through $A$, $B$ and $X$ also pass through $Y$?

solution.content: **(i) No.** For points $X$ and $Y$ on the same side of the chord $AB$, the angles $\angle AXB$ and $\angle AYB$ subtend the same arc $AB$. By the corollary of Theorem 9, all angles subtended by the same arc at points on the circle are equal. So $\angle AXB = \angle AYB$ always.

**(ii) Yes.** If $X$ and $Y$ are on opposite sides of $AB$, they subtend complementary arcs, and the angles are supplementary (they add to $180°$), not equal (unless both are $90°$). So equal angles imply $X$ and $Y$ are on the same side of $AB$.

**(iii) Yes.** By Theorem 10 (concyclicity), if the segment $AB$ subtends equal angles at two points $X$ and $Y$ on the same side of $AB$, then $A$, $B$, $X$, $Y$ all lie on the same circle. So the circle through $A$, $B$ and $X$ also passes through $Y$.

questions.answer: (i) No — angles in the same segment are equal. (ii) Yes. (iii) Yes — by the concyclicity theorem.
questions.notes: **Exam Tip:** Angles subtended by the same chord in the same segment are equal; in opposite segments they are supplementary.

questions.question: Find $x$ in Fig. 5.26. (A cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$ is shown with $\angle B = 100°$ and $\angle D = x$.)

solution.content: **Identify the quadrilateral:** $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$ lie on a circle, so $ABCD$ is a cyclic quadrilateral.
**Use the cyclic quadrilateral property:** Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral sum to $180°$: $$\angle B + \angle D = 180°$$

questions.notes: **Exam Tip:** In any cyclic quadrilateral, opposite angles are supplementary.
